column5: 14z-167: file a ticket - tenant attack records with facing rule +0xE = 5 are XORed into the victim's facing by vsavj's hit code (Killshread Summon (ES) moves Demitri on native only)
column10: Q3: resolved by WORK, and the finding was true: the p2step field was sampled as a BYTE (ff8964:b) while the counter +0x164 is a WORD (move.w $164(a6) at vs2 0x27050), so the instrument read the high byte and never registered the slide - the exclusion of the step table is WITHDRAWN. Re-traced as ff8964:w on both legs (build/x_family_14z167/step_routine_and_trace.txt, run7.log): the counter runs 0 -> 20 over 3928-3944 on BOTH legs with index +0x59 = 2 (the 80 px / 20 f list), and the step routine (vs2 0x27038, disassembled in the same file) picks the sign from +0x5D: tst.b $5d(a6); bne -> add, else neg.w. Native's rule-5 resolution writes 0 on the second wave, so the 20 steps are negated and Demitri slides 835 -> 755 toward Donovan; ours' XOR writes 4, nonzero, so the same steps are ADDED, away from Donovan, and his x holds at 835 (what holds it there - the stage edge - is not measured). The mover is therefore identified: the pushback step table, run identically on both legs, signed by the facing byte the two resolvers wrote differently. The ticket's text carries this corrected mechanism.

(a) NO GATE EVER OPENED THE SHIPPED FILE: the browser gate regenerated the page into its own workdir and drove that, and the sibling gate compared two fresh generations to each other, so "the shipped page is that generation" was assumed by everything. A hand-edited page, or a generator change landed without re-packaging, would have passed every check. FIXED TWO WAYS: test_applier_page.sh now regenerates EVERY platform dir's page and requires release/

/apply_release.html to be byte-identical to it (3/3 dirs), and test_applier_page_browser.sh now loads the SHIPPED file itself rather than a fresh one. (b) The fidelity leg runs through apply_node.mjs, which the page does not contain, so the page's own WIRING (page_shell.html's calls into the modules) was never compared with the tool of record. That gap is now NAMED in the gate's header and is covered from the other side: the browser gate drives the shipped page's real wiring — drop zone, radio, button — and checks the set key it prints, which is a SHA-1 over every member name and every member byte. Stated rather than overclaimed: the browser leg checks the set key, not member-for-member. Q4: TRUE, and the sharpest of the three: the "no network primitive" guarantee rested on a denylist of seven names with ONE control, and the page itself proved the blind spot by carrying `link.href = URL.createObjectURL(...)`, which the scan cannot see. A denylist cannot prove absence. RESOLVED BY CHANGING THE MECHANISM, not by lengthening the list: the page now carries a Content-Security-Policy of `default-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'` (plus frame/object/worker), so the BROWSER refuses every network primitive including the ones nobody enumerated, and the generator REFUSES to emit a page whose CSP is missing or weakened. The CSP is not decorative and was proven enforced the hard way: the browser gate's own driver, which lived inside the document, stopped working with "Failed to fetch" the moment the CSP landed — so the driver was rewritten as a SEPARATE page that iframes the shipped file, which keeps the page's real policy intact during the test instead of diluting it to be testable. The denylist is kept as an independent authoring-time check and was widened to the five primitives the checker named (RTCPeerConnection, WebTransport, Worker/SharedWorker, serviceWorker, setAttribute of a URL attribute, plus fetchLater, RTCDataChannel, new Image, geolocation), and a SECOND control `page-without-csp` now fires on a different mechanism from `page-with-fetch`. Q4's second limb — a refusal string present but unreachable — is also true: that leg IS a presence test, it now says so in the gate's own output and header, and the exercised cases went from four to SIX (a modified dump, a truncated dump, a missing dump, a dump with an extra member, a corrupted patch, a tampered manifest), each requiring both tools to refuse, both to name the same thing, and neither to write. ALSO MEASURED AND REJECTED while resolving Q4: Chrome's `--log-net-log` was tried as a direct "the page made zero network requests" measurement. It is NOT usable — the netlog records the BROWSER's own traffic (variations seed, component update, account listing, the default new-tab page), 15 non-file:// URLs on a default profile and still 9 with every background-networking flag disabled, none of them the page's. An assertion built on filtering Chrome's own requests would be an instrument that lies, so it was dropped rather than tuned. Q5: TRUE, and it is a PACKET-CONSTRUCTION error rather than a false claim. The claim attributes two closures to the maintainer and the artifact list contained no document carrying their words; the checker was right to refuse the attribution from what it was given. The words exist and are recorded verbatim, quoted, and dated in DECISIONS_HISTORY.md ("Ruled 2026-09-21 (14z-174) — #146 CLOSED", *"README is good enough for now. It may be improved, but it will be on the basis of more user feedback"*; and "Ruled 2026-09-21 (14z-174) — #144 CLOSED as MITIGATED, NOT ELIMINATED", *"Indeed, closeable with an explicit comment as mitigated not solved."*), and in each issue's closing comment. The lesson is the packet's: WHEN A PACKET ATTRIBUTES A DECISION, THE DECISION RECORD IS AN ARTIFACT. Recorded as a gotcha rather than left in this ledger row. The second limb — "the remaining M19 blocker list is empty but for #145" — is withdrawn as a claim of this packet: it is a consequence of the two closures plus the maintainer's own words about environments, and it belongs in the close's recommendation with those words quoted, not in a fidelity packet whose artifacts are code.

column5: re-freezing three emulator-tier expectations whose rows moved when the naming rigs changed at 14z-171/172
column10: Q1: TRUE and my claim was broader than my own evidence. The narrative named BOTH 14z-171 and 14z-172 as causes for killshread_es; 14z-172 cannot reach it — name_moves.py:421 pins donovan part 12's first event "far" and line 697 states that a far first event pins at FIRST_EVENT-40 = 2560, already past the round start, so those 35 parts do not move. The measurement had already said so and I did not listen to it: the captured diff is SIX rows in which only `stock` changes, 8 -> 9, which is 14z-171's per-event top-up and nothing else. The checker's point about the top-up's inertness argument resting on test_move_naming.sh, which skips part 12, is also correct — and that premise IS now tested directly on part 12, by the attribution: restoring the rig files AND tools/name_moves.py to e3f7537c makes the gate pass against its existing frozen rows, one variable, tree restored and sha256-verified. Every carrier of the two-cause wording is corrected. Q2: the finding is sound given the claim, and the CLAIM IS WRONG — withdrawn as a statement of fact. hp, white and cls do NOT move. Paired row by row rather than read as a unified diff, the six removed rows and six added rows are identical in move, frame, cls, hp and white; only stock differs. My earlier reading compared a removed row against a DIFFERENT added row (+31 against +88) and manufactured a damage change that does not exist. So no value a player could feel moved, and no capture is owed. The same pairing was applied to the other two tables and reported in full: reaction_class_live 13 rows with leg/direction/pc/value UNCHANGED, defense_row_reads 5 rows with leg/pc/kind/identity/value UNCHANGED; only count columns moved in both. Q3: TRUE, verified in the code, and ACCEPTED as a known limitation by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-22 (option 1 of three put to them). name_moves.py:802 pokes ff8509 := 09 sixty frames before every event and test_killshread_es.sh:50 samples ff8509 as the `stock` column, so that column reads the rig's own poke back; audit_defense_row_reads taps RTAP="ff8782,2;ff8b82,2", exactly the bytes name_moves.py:768,770 poke at 1400/1450/1500. The consequence is recorded rather than glossed: the stock column records the RIG, not the engine's meter, and [VSP-170]'s ES-versus-normal stock-drop discriminator is neutralised in this rig by the per-event top-up. Written into the gate's own header and into tests/expected/PROVENANCE.md so the next reader is not misled by a column that looks like a measurement. The maintainer's wider instruction — "ticket to qualify all gates in the future because either the gates are moving silently or they never were validated and in both cases that's a lot of both uncertainty and wasted time" — is a new ticket, because this sitting found five gates dead for four days, three expectations stale behind moved rigs, one control that never ran inside its timeout, and one column that never measured what it appeared to.

column5: the 14z-174 close: the M19 release, the eight reds and what the close record claims about them
column10: Q1: TRUE and accepted. tools/audit_lane_carry.py HARDCODES each lane's subject list and reads ci_emulator.tsv only for gate NAMES; it omits tests/replays, which ci_emulator.tsv makes a load-bearing operand of a mister gate, and ci_emulator.tsv itself, which carries every row's args and timeouts. So "every subject it depends on is byte-unchanged" was asserted over a list that could not see part of the answer. THE M19 CONCLUSION NEVERTHELESS HOLDS, and it is verified BY HAND over exactly the omitted paths rather than argued: tests/replays has 0 files changed since cf4dfd86, and the single ci_emulator.tsv row that moved is test_release_binaries, a MAME-lane row. The answer was right and the method did not earn it, which is the finding. Three corrections landed rather than a promise: the tool's docstring now states outright that its lists are hardcoded and names both omissions; its MAY CARRY verdict PRINTS the caveat and the unchecked paths, so a reader of stdout cannot take it as stronger than it is; and widening the lists plus the control that reconciles them against the registry is GitHub #171, not deferred silently. Q2: N-A as answered, and undisturbed. Q3: TRUE and already ruled. test_killshread_es samples ff8509 while the rig pokes it, so the stock column reads the rig's own poke back, and the attribution's two legs run through that same rig, so a rig defect would make them agree. This is recorded in the gate's own header, in tests/expected/PROVENANCE.md and in the 2026-09-22 ruling, which re-froze that column in full knowledge of what it is ("Option 1"). What the attribution DOES establish is narrower and is stated as such: it separates the rig's CONTRIBUTION from the subject's, not the rig's correctness. Qualifying it is #171. Q4: TRUE. The failure mode "the hardcoded subject list is incomplete or stale" had no control, and the only demonstration exercised paths that were already listed. Nothing yet reconciles the list against the registry, and that control is the substance of #171 rather than something to bolt on at a session close. Until it exists the tool now refuses to overstate itself in its own output, which is the mitigation available tonight, and the release decision it informed was independently checked by hand. THE ROW THAT OVERSTATED IT IS CORRECTED IN PLACE: STATE.md said the tool "reads each lane's subjects from the ruled cadence split in ci_emulator.tsv", which is not what the code does; the sentence now says what it does, names both omissions, and records that the M19 carry was verified by hand. Re-grepped: no live document makes the old claim, and the only remaining copy is the rule-checker's own staged snapshot, which is evidence and is not rewritten.
